title: auricula-ursi pedemontana subsp. iberica
intro: Auricula-ursi pedemontana subsp. iberica, commonly known as Bearberry, is a plant species belonging to the heather family (Ericaceae) and is native to the Iberian Peninsula. It has been traditionally used for its health benefits, including its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties, which can aid in treating urinary tract infections, diarrhea, and other gastrointestinal issues. The therapeutic actions of Bearberry include its ability to act as a diuretic, an antiseptic, and an anti-inflammatory agent, making it an effective treatment for various conditions. The bioactive constituents of Bearberry include arbutin, a glycosidic compound responsible for its antimicrobial properties, as well as other phenolic compounds such as flavonoids and phenolic acids.
